what_it_is.prose: Antrix is the original commercial arm of ISRO, incorporated in 1992 to market ISRO launch services, satellite transponder capacity, remote-sensing imagery, and mission-support services to international customers. It has enabled launches for satellites belonging to multiple countries (Israel TecSAR, Algeria AlSat, European SPOT series, etc.) and earned ~₹1,790 Cr revenue in 2015-16 through launch of commercial satellites and data products. From 2019 onward, Antrix's commercial launch-services mandate has been progressively transferred to NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), the new DOS PSU. Antrix is best known internationally for the Devas-Antrix S-band controversy: a fraudulent 2005 agreement to lease S-band spectrum to Devas Multimedia, annulled by Government of India in 2011; ICC arbitration (2015) ordered Antrix to pay $562.5M+interest to Devas (later set aside by Supreme Court of India in 2022 on grounds of fraud; upheld by US Supreme Court Jun 2025).

rows.india_status: Antrix has provided commercial launch services since 1999 for customer satellites (Israeli TecSAR, European SPOT, etc.); 319 customer satellites from 33 countries launched onboard PSLV by Jun 2019 through Antrix. Most commercial launch mandate transferred to NSIL post-2019
Antrix leases ISRO communication-satellite transponders to private/DTH/VSAT operators and sells IRS remote-sensing imagery (~$20-25M annual revenue historically)
